mainEntity.name: Does a turnkey metal home take less time to complete than finishing a shell?

acceptedAnswer.text: A turnkey build usually finishes faster overall because a general contractor runs trades sequentially without long gaps between framing, rough-ins, and drywall. Erecting a metal building shell often takes only a few weeks once the engineered slab cures. However, when owners take over the interior after the shell stage, finishing the home frequently stretches out over a year or more due to personal schedule constraints, subcontractor availability, and phased cash flow.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, turnkey builds are usually faster overall because professional trades are scheduled back-to-back, whereas self-finished shells often face personal scheduling delays.
